Thanks Daniel — great context. Short answer: we can meet your targets with a combined approach (int8/4-bit on lighter sequences, targeted KV prefill, and a weekly tuning cadence during ramp). I attached a condensed "tuning-runbook_v1.pdf" and a comparison CSV that shows perf vs. quality tradeoffs across our recommended profiles for your baseline prompt set. Key proposals: 

- Quantization: run two parallel profiles during canary (int8 + gptq-4bit) and keep fp16 as fallback. Start with int8 for production routes that are latency-sensitive; enable gptq-4bit on low-cost batch routes.
- Batching: steady-state continuous batching with max window 60ms for P50-bound routes; higher batching for throughput-only routes.
- Cache priming: yes — seed KV cache with top-50 user flows and prime during low-traffic windows (daily prefill job). Use TTL of 4 hours for long-tail items, longer for static prompts.
- Routing: two-tier routing policy -- (1) latency-first for web UI (p50 target), (2) cost-first for async endpoints. Automatic fallback to fp16 when quality/regression thresholds are hit.

Suggested cadence and owners for the next 6 weeks: 
Week 0: profile collection (Veridian ops + Redwood instrumentation) — owner: Priya Shah
Week 1: baseline canary (A/B int8 vs fp16) — owner: Marissa Cole (CS)
Week 2-4: iterative tuning (batch windows, cache TTL, route weights) — owner: Karthik Iyer (solutions)
Week 5: final signoff and rollout plan (Redwood + Veridian) — owner: Vivek Kulkarni (AM)

I'll sync this into the mutual action plan spreadsheet. If that looks good I can schedule the 30-min kickoff with your infra team.

Best,

Priya — some quick answers and concrete numbers so you can staff the sprint:

- Canary plan: canary traffic should be 3–5% for 48 hours, with automated monitoring and a scheduled safety rollback window.
